results.title: Searching across multiple languages
results.content: # Searching across multiple languages. Discover how easy it can be to implement advanced multilingual search and give your users the seamless, relevant results they deserve—regardless of language. In today's interconnected world, many applications need to handle content in multiple languages. Meilisearch offers powerful capabilities for multilingual search, combining intelligent language handling with specialized models for optimal relevance. This guide will walk you through setting up multilingual search with Meilisearch, covering both full-text and semantic search approaches. # Why multilingual search matters. 2. Improved user experience: Provide relevant results regardless of the language used in queries or content. Now, let's explore how Meilisearch makes multilingual search a breeze. ## Full-text search: intelligent language handling. At its core, Meilisearch excels at handling diverse languages out of the box. When you add documents to your Meilisearch index, the engine automatically detects the language of each field. This means you don't need to specify languages manually in most cases - Meilisearch will handle it for you. Meilisearch will automatically detect and properly handle the different languages in each field, ensuring accurate search results across your multilingual content. ### Specifying languages for specific fields. While automatic detection works well in most cases, you might want more control over language handling for certain fields. Meilisearch allows you to specify languages for particular attributes using the `localizedAttributes` setting. # Semantic search: Enhancing multilingual relevance. While full-text search works well for many multilingual scenarios, semantic search can provide even better results, especially for complex queries or when dealing with nuanced meanings across languages. Meilisearch supports various embedding models for semantic search, offering powerful auto-embedding capabilities. Meilisearch handles the generation and storage of embeddings automatically, seamlessly integrating them into your search experience. These models are designed to understand and represent meaning across multiple languages, leading to more relevant search results in multilingual contexts. One excellent option for multilingual semantic search is the Cohere Multilingual embedding model. Cohere's model is particularly adept at understanding context and nuance in different languages, making it an ideal choice for diverse, multilingual content. Ready to get started with multilingual search? Typesense review: powerful search engine with flexible configuration, but Meilisearch offers simpler setup.

results.title: How to translate metadata for better multilingual SEO
results.content: Metadata, including title tags and meta descriptions, is often the first thing users see in search results. Metadata sends signals to search engines about the content of a webpage and helps them display the most relevant version to users based on keywords, language, and location. In the context of a multilingual site, poorly translated metadata can lead to misperceptions, lower local search rankings, and decreased clicks from users. Meanwhile, technical metadata that remains in the original language can be confusing when shared on social media or search engines, which display page snippets. These practices help the metadata appear more relevant in local search engines and ensure the user experience remains consistent across all site language versions. Instead of just translating keywords from the original language, it is important to understand how users in the target market search. By understanding local keywords, the metadata you create will be more in line with user behavior and can increase the potential for clicks from search results. Customizing metadata to the local language style not only helps visibility, but also increases user trust and comfort when viewing your site in search results. Errors in technical configuration, such as inconsistent use of hreflang or not including all language versions, can cause well-translated metadata to still not appear optimally in local search results. Managing metadata in a multilingual SEO project can be complex, especially if many pages need to be translated and optimized. Linguise automatically detects metadata such as title and meta description on each page, and translates them in real-time into multiple languages. URL management is an important aspect of maintaining metadata consistency and multilingual SEO effectiveness, as metadata such as page titles, descriptions, and image alt texts will lose their relevance if they are associated with URLs that do not match the language or cultural context of the user. Linguise automatically generates hreflang tags for each language version so that search engines understand which version of content is relevant for each user based on their language and location. Optimized metadata helps improve site visibility in local search results and ensures that users from different regions find your site relevant, professional, and worth visiting.
